title: ALEXANDER, William. PICTURESQUE REPRESENTATIONS of the Dress and Manners of the Chinese.
description: ALEXANDER, William. PICTURESQUE REPRESENTATIONS of the Dress and Manners of the Chinese. Illustrated in Fifty Coloured Engravings, With Descriptions. Octavo, 50 handcoloured engraved plates, some spotting and handling, broken binding of old half calf. London, John Murray, 1814. Estimate $400/600

title: ANSON, George. A VOYAGE ROUND THE WORLD in the years MDCCXL, I, II, III, IV, compiled from Papers and other materials of the Right Hon.
description: ANSON, George. A VOYAGE ROUND THE WORLD in the years MDCCXL, I, II, III, IV, compiled from Papers and other materials of the Right Hon. George Lord Anson... By Richard Walter. Octavo, three folding engraved charts, the chart of South America standing proud and split along one fold, five folding engraved views, front pastedown with name blacked out in ink, rebacked contemporary calf. London, Knapton, 1748. Seventh octavo edition of this hugely popular eighteenth-century voyage account, many times reprinted after its first publication in quarto in 1748. Estimate $180/240

title: ARMITAGE, Lieut. A.B. TWO YEARS IN THE ANTARCTIC, being a narrative of the British National Antarctic Expedition.
description: ARMITAGE, Lieut. A.B. TWO YEARS IN THE ANTARCTIC, being a narrative of the British National Antarctic Expedition. Octavo, plates, illustrations, folding map, half-title foxed, original pictorial cloth, head of spine splitting. London, Edward Arnold, 1905. + BROWN, R.N. Rudmose. THE POLAR REGIONS. Octavo, original cloth, gilt, Ingleton copy with bookplate. London, Methuen & Co., 1927. Estimate $200/300

title: BERNACCHI, Louis Charles.
description: BERNACCHI, Louis Charles. TO THE SOUTH POLAR REGIONS: Expedition of 1898 – 1900. Octavo, with two folding maps, folding panorama, numerous other illustrations in the text (many full-page), with 4 pages of advertisements, title-page printed in red and black, original dark blue cloth (barely canted), free endpapers shadowed, with the armorial bookplate of Herbert Massey, a fine copy and uncommon thus. London, Hurst &Blackett, 1901. First edition: participant’s account of the Antarctic cruise of the Southern Cross under the leadership of C. E. Borchgrevink. This was the first expedition to winter in the Antarctic. In his eighth year, in 1884, Belgian-born Bernacchi arrived in Tasmania with his family; he was naturalised in 1886. Bernacchi joined the Southern Cross expedition as physicist and astronomer and became the first Australian to work and winter in Antarctica. In 1900 he was made a Fellow of the Royal Geographical Society and was awarded the Society’s Peek Grant. In 1901-4 he served as physicist with Scott’s first Antarctic Expedition. Renard, 110; Spence, 124. Estimate $1500/2000

title: BLIGH. WOODARD, David.
description: BLIGH. WOODARD, David. THE NARRATIVE OF CAPTAIN DAVID WOODARD AND FOUR SEAMEN, who lost their ship while in a boat at sea, and surrendered themselves up to the Malays in the Island of Celebes. Octavo, plates (some staining) and two folding maps (with repaired tears), staining to preliminaries and final leaves, old worn half morocco, neat modern rebacking. London, J. Johnson, 1804. First edition: very scarce. Woodard’s narrative of his shipwreck and capture by the Malays. An appendix includes accounts of other shipwrecks and maritime misadventure, as a warning to mariners, including the Bounty mutiny, the ‘Antelope’ and ‘Pandora’ wrecks, and the frightening experiences of the crew of the ‘Shah Hormazier’ in Torres Strait. Ferguson, 399. Estimate $200/400

title: BORCHGREVINK, Carsten E. FIRST ON THE ANTARCTIC CONTINENT: being an Account of the British Antarctic Expedition, 1898 –
description: BORCHGREVINK, Carsten E. FIRST ON THE ANTARCTIC CONTINENT: being an Account of the British Antarctic Expedition, 1898 – 1900. Octavo, with photogravure frontispiece portrait, three folding tinted maps, numerous illustrations in the text (many full-page), and pp. 32 (advertisements dated in code “1.01” on the first page), original silver and gilt pictorial cloth, front board lettered in gilt and with an attractive gilt and silver block of a ship in ice, top edge gilt, others uncut: a fine copy. London, Newnes, 1901. First edition (primary binding). This is the leader and organiser’s account of the Antarctic cruise of the Southern Cross, the first expedition to winter in the Antarctic continent and the first to use dogs in the Antarctic. The party made first landings on Coulman Island and Ross Island, built a hut at Cape Adare, and were the first to travel over the Ross Ice Shelf, establishing a new furthest south. Louis Bernacchi was a member of the expedition and wrote his own account of it, also published in 1901. Renard, 152; Rosove, 45.A1; Spence, 151. Estimate $800/1200 Lots 4 and 6

title: BOUGAINVILLE, Louis Antoine de.
description: BOUGAINVILLE, Louis Antoine de. A VOYAGE ROUND THE WORLD. Performed by Order of His Most Christian Majesty, in the Years 1766, 1767, 17687, and 1769… Quarto, with five folding charts and a folding plate, near contemporary calf (rubbed), rebacked preserving spine (gilt). London, Printed for J. Nourse and T. Davies, 1772. First English edition. Translated by Georg Forster – although unacknowledged – with an introduction and notes by his father, Johann Reinhold Forster. Although Forster praises the work in his introduction (“a learned, intelligent, and judicious traveller”), he adds that he has “partially vindicated the British nation where we thought the author had been unjustly partial”. Davidson, pp. 96-7; Hill 2, 165; Kroepelien, 113; Sabin, 6869. Estimate $3000/5000

title: BRETON, J.B.J. CHINA, its Costume, Arts, Manufactures, &c.
description: BRETON, J.B.J. CHINA, its Costume, Arts, Manufactures, &c. edited principally from the originals in the cabinet of the late M. Bertin, with observations, historical and literary… in four volumes. Four volumes in two, small octavo, 4 engraved hand-coloured frontispieces and 76 fine hand-coloured stipple-and-line engraved plates, the first three plates and seven leaves of vol. 3 stained, contemporary straight-grained burgundy morocco, the boards with separate gilt and blind-stamped borders, all edges gilt. London, Howlett and Brimmer, 1824. Estimate $300/500

title: BROWN, R.N. Rudmose, R.C. MOSSMAN, and Dr.
description: BROWN, R.N. Rudmose, R.C. MOSSMAN, and Dr. J.H.H. PIRIE. THE VOYAGE OF THE “SCOTIA”: Being the Record of a Voyage of Exploration in Antarctic Seas. By Three of the Staff. Octavo, with a large coloured folding map (the verso with amateurish strengthening and repaired with old paper tape), 2 other maps, 59 plates, a little shaken in original grey cloth, spine and front board decorated and lettered in white and black, top edge gilt, blue endpapers, rubbed, head and foot of spine wearing, spine lettering dulled as often. Edinburgh, William Blackwood and Sons, 1906. First edition: with the bookplate of Herbert Dyce Murphy, the Australian adventurer and member of Mawson’s team on the Australasian Antarctic Expedition of 1911-14. Estimate $600/900

title: COOK, James. A COMPLETE SET OF THE VOYAGE ACCOUNTS. Comprising: Hawkesworth, John.
description: COOK, James. A COMPLETE SET OF THE VOYAGE ACCOUNTS. Comprising: Hawkesworth, John. An Account of the Voyages undertaken… for making Discoveries in the Southern Hemisphere, and successively performed by Commodore Byron, Captain Wallis, Captain Carteret, and Captain Cook... drawn up from the journals which were kept by the several commanders, and from the papers of Joseph Banks, Esq., three volumes, quarto, first edition, London, 1773; COOK, James. A Voyage towards the South Pole and Round the World, performed in His Majesty’s Ships the Resolution and Adventure in the years 1772, 1773, 1774, and 1775, two volumes, quarto, first edition, London, 1777; and COOK, James and James KING. A Voyage to the Pacific Ocean... for making Discoveries in the Northern Hemisphere... in His Majesty’s Ships the Resolution and Discovery, three volumes, quarto (text) second and preferred edition, and folio atlas of charts and plates, London, 1785. Eight quarto volumes of text, and a folio atlas volume to the third voyage, with all engraved plates and maps, several small sealed tears, many of the double-page South Pole plates on stubs for ease of opening, plate 22 in atlas with repaired full height tear, early owner’s name partly erased from imprint of first voyage first volume, overall a fine set with only very occasional offsetting, foxing or spotting of the text or plates, uniformly bound in chocolate half morocco by Lewis & Harris (Bath). London, W. Strahan, and T. Cadell, [third voyage: H. Hughs, for G. Nicol, and T. Cadell], 1773 – 1785. A complete set of the official accounts of Cook’s three voyages around the world, the cornerstone of any collection of modern voyages. “Captain Cook’s three great voyages form the basis of any collection of Pacific books. In these three voyages Cook did more to clarify the geographical knowledge of the southern hemisphere than all his predecessors together had done. He was the first really scientific navigator, and his voyages made great contributions to many fields of knowledge…” (Hill). Forbes, 62 (“arguably the single most important book on the Hawaiian Islands”); Hocken, pp. 10-11, 15-6, and 23-4; Holmes, 5, 24, and 47; Kroepelien, 535; PMM, 223; Renard, 369; Rosove, 77.A1; Sabin, 30934, 16245, and 16250, Wantrup (2025), 5.05, 6.01, and 12.14 Estimate $12,000/15,000 Lot 10

title: COOK. BANKS, Sir Joseph and Daniel Solander.
description: COOK. BANKS, Sir Joseph and Daniel Solander. ILLUSTRATIONS OF THE BOTANY OF CAPTAIN COOK’S VOYAGE around the world in H.M.S. Endeavour in 1768-71... With determinations by James Britten… Three parts, elephant folio, 320 lithographed plates (numbered to 318), and three folding maps, with titlepages and text to each part, rebound with new endpapers in the original cloth-backed portfolios, printed labels on front boards, spine labels worn and one lacking. London, Printed by Order of the Trustees of the British Museum, 1900 - 1901 - 1905. Rare: one of 300 sets, this was the first publication of the illustrations prepared by Banks and Solander on the botany of Cook’s first voyage. Banks had copper plates engraved between 1772 and 1784 but these were never published and on Banks’s death the copper plates were deposited with the British Museum (Natural History). The earliest attempt at publishing a substantial selection of the plates did not eventuate until this magnificent publication of three portfolios in 1900-5. Nissen BBI, 74. Estimate $3000/5000

title: COOK. KIPPIS, Andrew. THE LIFE OF CAPTAIN JAMES COOK. Octavo, early tree calf, later rebacked and recornered.
description: COOK. KIPPIS, Andrew. THE LIFE OF CAPTAIN JAMES COOK. Octavo, early tree calf, later rebacked and recornered. Dublin, H. Chamberlaine, W. Colles (and others), 1788. The rare Dublin edition of Kippis’s great biography of Cook, the first biography of the explorer. This Dublin edition was published immediately after the London edition and, as is often the case with the Dublin piracies, it is much rarer than the original. Kippis had access to Admiralty sources as well as documents belonging to Joseph Banks, and attempted a full account of Cook’s public life. He includes a long account of Cook’s death from Samwell’s rare pamphlet (which Kippis had helped to be published): “I procured its publication, that, if any objections should be made to it, I might be able to notice them in my own work. As the narrative hath continued for more than two years unimpeached and uncontradicted, I esteem myself fully authorised to insert it in this place, as containing the most complete and authentic account of the melancholy catastrophe, which, at Owhyee, befell our illustrious navigator and Commander ...”. Beddie, 34 (in error, corrected by Forbes); Forbes, 152; Hill 2, 936, Kroepelien, 648. Estimate $600/900

title: CHARCOT, Dr. Jean. THE VOYAGE OF THE “WHY NOT?” IN THE ANTARCTIC. The Journal of the Second French South Polar Expeditio
description: CHARCOT, Dr. Jean. THE VOYAGE OF THE “WHY NOT?” IN THE ANTARCTIC. The Journal of the Second French South Polar Expedition, 1908 – 1910. English Version by Philip Walsh. Large octavo, folding frontispiece, plates, full-page map, original gilt-pictorial blue-grey cloth, gilt vignette of the “Pourquoi Pas?” on the front board, penguin on spine in white, spine and front board lettered in gilt. London, New York, and Toronto, Hodder and Stoughton, [1911]. First Edition in English. Charcot’s account of the Second French South Polar Expedition is one of the classics of the heroic age of Antarctic exploration. Apart from the vast quantity of scientific data collected, Charcot discovered several islands and charted over 1250 miles of uncharted Antarctic coast. Renard 296; Rosove, 67.A1; Spence 262. Estimate $400/600

title: DAVIS, John F. THE CHINESE, a general description of the Empire of China and its inhabitants.
description: DAVIS, John F. THE CHINESE, a general description of the Empire of China and its inhabitants. Two volumes, duodecimo, illustrated, original embossed cloth (marked). London, Charles Knight, 1836. With the signature (mistakenly on the rear endpaper) in 1840 of G. S. Kingston (surveyor with Col. William Light). + Two mid-century works on China: Jones, Life and Travel in Tartary, and Prandi, Memoirs of Father Ripa. Estimate $200/300

title: DAVIS, John King. WITH THE “AURORA” IN THE ANTARCTIC 1911 – 1914. Quarto, plates, maps and illustrations, frontispiece r
description: DAVIS, John King. WITH THE “AURORA” IN THE ANTARCTIC 1911 – 1914. Quarto, plates, maps and illustrations, frontispiece reinserted (ragged outer margin and with a spot of adhesion at gutter), a little pale foxing, original dark blue buckram, gilt vignette on front board, spine lettering lost. London, Andrew Melrose, Ltd., [1919]. First edition Estimate $300/500

title: DOOLITTLE, Rev. Justus.
description: DOOLITTLE, Rev. Justus. SOCIAL LIFE OF THE CHINESE, a daguerreotype of daily life in China… edited and revised by the Rev. Paxton Hood. Octavo, illustrated, full calf, marbled endpapers and edges. London, Sampson Low, Son, and Marston, 1868. + Four works on China. Estimate $100/200

title: EDGE-PARTINGTON, James.
description: EDGE-PARTINGTON, James. AN ALBUM OF THE WEAPONS, Tools, Ornaments, Articles of Dress of the Natives of the Pacific Islands. Two volumes, oblong quarto, plates, cloth gilt. London, The Holland Press, 1969. Facsimile edition. Estimate $200/300

title: EDGE-PARTINGTON, James.
description: EDGE-PARTINGTON, James. AN ALBUM OF THE WEAPONS, Tools, Ornaments, Articles of Dress &c. of the Natives of the Pacific Islands. Third Series. Oblong folio, 225 lithographed sheets, complete with 7 leaves of Additional Notes (title-leaf toned), a fine copy, loose as issued in the original cloth box with metal clasp, pictorial title label to cover. London, issued for private circulation by James Edge-Partington & Charles Heape, 1898. Edition limited to 175 numbered copies, initialled by Edge-Partington and Heape. Edge-Partington’s three year expedition to the Pacific in 1879-1882, which he recounted in Random Rot (1883), was the basis for the first two series of this Album. This third series was issued following his subsequent visit to the region. A serious collector of artefacts, and a noted collector of books, he was a donor to the British Museum, where he assisted in documenting their South Seas collection. Estimate $1500/3000

title: ELLIS, Henry. JOURNAL OF THE PROCEEDINGS OF THE LATE EMBASSY TO CHINA, Comprising a correct narrative of the public tran
description: ELLIS, Henry. JOURNAL OF THE PROCEEDINGS OF THE LATE EMBASSY TO CHINA, Comprising a correct narrative of the public transactions of the Embassy, of the voyage to and from China, and of the journey from the mouth of the Pei-Ho to the return to Canton. Interspersed with Observations upon the face of the Country, the Polity, moral Character, and Manners of the Chinese Nation. The whole illustrated by maps and drawings. Quarto, engraved portrait frontispiece, one folding map (paper strengthening on verso to correct a corner tear, two full-page maps (browned), seven fine handcoloured aquatint plates, with the errata leaf, armorial bookplate, contemporary half calf and marbled boards, rebacked with remnants of the earlier spine, marbled endpapers and edges. London, John Murray, 1817. First edition. Abbey, Travel, 536; Hill, 542. Estimate $600/800 Lot 19

title: HURLEY, James Francis (Frank).
description: HURLEY, James Francis (Frank). ARGONAUTS OF THE SOUTH: Being a Narrative of Voyagings and Polar Seas and Adventures in the Antarctic with Sir Douglas Mawson and Sir Ernest Shackleton. With 75 illustrations and maps. Octavo, with plates and two folding maps, original dark green cloth, boards flecked at margins and recoloured, gilt, top edge gilt, others uncut, photographic endpapers. New York and London, G.P. Putnam’s Sons The Knickerbocker Press, 1925. First edition. Hurley was official photographer with Mawson’s Australasian Antarctic Expedition, 1911-1913 as well as with Shackleton’s 1914-1917 expedition; later again he joined Mawson’s 1929 B.A.N.Z.A.R.E. voyage. This book describes his experiences in the Antarctic with Mawson and Shackleton, 19111917. Renard, 768; Rosove, 178.A1; Spence, 615 (title mistranscribed). Estimate $200/400

title: KELLERMAN, Annette. FAIRY TALES OF THE SOUTH SEAS. and other Stories.
description: KELLERMAN, Annette. FAIRY TALES OF THE SOUTH SEAS. and other Stories. Octavo, plates, diffuse foxing, bright original cloth with pictorial dustwrapper (pale staining mostly on spine). London, Sampson Low, [1926] Estimate $100/200

title: MAWSON, Douglas. THE HOME OF THE BLIZZARD: Being the Story of the Australasian Antarctic Expedition, 1911 – 1914. Two vo
description: MAWSON, Douglas. THE HOME OF THE BLIZZARD: Being the Story of the Australasian Antarctic Expedition, 1911 – 1914. Two volumes, thick octavo, titles printed in two colours, coloured and black & white plates (some folding), illustrations, maps (three folding maps in pocket at rear of volume II), front free endpaper with 2 cm. loss and thinning at head, first blank showing adhesion damage at head and with modern clipping pasted to verso, half title with old sellotape mark at head, original silver pictorial dark blue cloth: with, loosely inserted, a second copy of the portrait frontispiece signed and dated by Mawson in 1916. London, William Heinemann, 1915. First edition. The classic account of Mawson’s first expedition, an epic of endurance which, together with his subsequent work in the Antarctic, forms the most significant basis to Australia’s claim to its extensive Antarctic Territory. Mawson’s book includes a self-effacing account of his epic journey across five hundred kilometres of Adelie Land in 1912, without a tent and most of his food, one of the great feats of human endurance. Estimate $1000/1500

title: MAWSON, Douglas. GEOGRAPHICAL NARRATIVE AND CARTOGRAPHY. Quarto, plates and folding maps, original wrappers.
description: MAWSON, Douglas. GEOGRAPHICAL NARRATIVE AND CARTOGRAPHY. Quarto, plates and folding maps, original wrappers. Sydney, A. H. Pettifer, Acting Government Printer, 1942. Scientific Reports, Australasian Antarctic Expedition 1911-14, Series A, Vol. I. Estimate $200/300

title: MILL, Hugh Robert. THE SIEGE OF THE SOUTH POLE: The Story of Antarctic Exploration.
description: MILL, Hugh Robert. THE SIEGE OF THE SOUTH POLE: The Story of Antarctic Exploration. Octavo, folding maps (one coloured), other maps and plates, the large folding map with three pale stained spots and strengthened with paper on verso repairing several torn folds, uncut in the original gilt-decorated green cloth (front board bright, spine dulled). London, Alston Rivers, 1905. First edition, first issue. An important and comprehensive work: “a classic – the finest overview of Antarctic exploration ever written and an essential reference work” (Rosove). Estimate $300/500

title: O’CONNELL, James F. A RESIDENCE OF ELEVEN YEARS in New Holland and the Caroline Islands: Being the Adventures of James F. O’Connell.
description: O’CONNELL, James F. A RESIDENCE OF ELEVEN YEARS in New Holland and the Caroline Islands: Being the Adventures of James F. O’Connell. Edited from his Verbal Narration. Duodecimo, frontispiece, modern half calf and marbled boards. Boston, B.B. Mussey, 1841. Born in Dublin, O’Connell travelled as a cabin boy on a convict transport to Port Jackson. He spent some years in New South Wales, most notably accompanying Oxley on a six months’ exploring expedition. In a later voyage he was shipwrecked in the Carolines, where he spent more than five years. His description is considered the first extensive ethnographic account of the island of Ponape. He was ‘rescued’ by the American schooner Spy and, after some vicissitudes, returned to New York in 1835. Ferguson, 3268. Estimate $400/600

title: OLIPHANT, Laurence. NARRATIVE OF THE EARL OF ELGIN’S MISSION TO CHINA AND JAPAN, in the years 1857, ‘58, ‘59. Two volume
description: OLIPHANT, Laurence. NARRATIVE OF THE EARL OF ELGIN’S MISSION TO CHINA AND JAPAN, in the years 1857, ‘58, ‘59. Two volumes, octavo, 20 colour lithograph plates, five folding maps, a fine set in early half calf, marbled endpapers and edges. Edinburgh and London, William Blackwood and Sons, 1859. Oliphant, a British adventurer and diplomat, was Lord Elgin’s private secretary on this mission designed to bring about the end of the Anglo-Chinese War. “He was present at the bombardment of Canton and participated in signing of the treaty of Tientsin… Oliphant then proceeded with the mission to Japan, landing first at Nagasaki then at Edo Bay where the Furious became the first foreign ship to anchor since the opening of Japan to foreign trade”. Howgego (1850-1940), 01. Estimate $400/600

title: PHILLIP, Governor Arthur.
description: PHILLIP, Governor Arthur. THE VOYAGE OF GOVERNOR PHILLIP TO BOTANY BAY; with an Account of the Establishment of the Colonies of Port Jackson and Norfolk Island... to which are added the Journals of Lieuts. Shortland, Watts, Ball and Capt. Marshall. Quarto, engraved plates and charts, defective frontispiece, London, John Stockdale, 1789. First edition of the foundation book for New South Wales. Ferguson, 47; Wantrup (2023), 5. Estimate $1200/1500

title: PONTING, Herbert. THE GREAT WHITE SOUTH being an account of experiences with Captain Scott’s South Pole Expedition… Octa
description: PONTING, Herbert. THE GREAT WHITE SOUTH being an account of experiences with Captain Scott’s South Pole Expedition… Octavo, with 95 plates, full-page map, traces of pale foxing, original cloth, spine sunned. London, Duckworth, 1921. First edition and quite scarce. Estimate $200/300

title: PRIESTLEY, Raymond E. ANTARCTIC ADVENTURE: Scott’s Northern Party.
description: PRIESTLEY, Raymond E. ANTARCTIC ADVENTURE: Scott’s Northern Party. Octavo, with all plates and folding maps, line-drawings in the text, the last leaf of the contents (pp. 17/8 is a cancel as in all copies noted hitherto), free front endpaper removed, original light blue cloth, spine and front board lettered and decorated in silver, top edge gilt, others rough trimmed, spine fading towards grey as usual, a few other light marks and creases to the cloth. London: T. Fisher Unwin, 1914. First edition: the Northern Party under V.L.A. Campbell were forced to winter over when the Terra Nova failed to pick them up. The book is very scarce: “Spence states that many copies were destroyed in a fire at the publisher’s warehouse, a report since verified from hand-written notes of the Author” (Renard), while Rosove records Priestley’s statement that 1000 copies were destroyed. Renard, 1254; Rosove, 256.A1; Spence 939. Estimate $600/800

title: ROSS, Sir James Clark.
description: ROSS, Sir James Clark. A VOYAGE OF DISCOVERY AND RESEARCH in the Southern and Antarctic Regions, during the years 1839 – 43. Two volumes, octavo, with 16 plates and maps (three folding), other engravings in the text, advertisements dated January 1847, uncut in the original gilt-decorated blue cloth, rebacked retaining original spines, new endpapers. London, John Murray, 1847. First edition of the official narrative of Ross’s expedition to the Antarctic in the Erebus and Terror. Ferguson, 4636; Hill 2, 1487; Renard, 1328; Rosove, 276. A1; Spence, 993. Estimate $1500/3000

title: SCOTT, Robert Falcon. THE VOYAGE OF THE ‘DISCOVERY’. Two volumes, thick octavo, with all coloured plates (some double-pa
description: SCOTT, Robert Falcon. THE VOYAGE OF THE ‘DISCOVERY’. Two volumes, thick octavo, with all coloured plates (some double-page) and black & white plates, maps and folding charts), the first volume bumped at foot of spine and with loss of gilt on the front board vignette, both volumes showing the cloth renewed with blue wash, original cloth, top edge gilt. London, Smith, Elder, & Co., 1905. Second impression. The official account of Scott’s first expedition and one of the great works of exploration literature. The British Nation Antarctic Expedition of 190104 was primarily a scientific and surveying expedition aimed at re-establishing the British Navy at the forefront of Polar exploration. Scott’s Discovery expedition was the first detailed and truly elaborate scientific exploration of the continent and set a high standard of achievement for the expeditions that followed. The fine coloured plates are after watercolours by Edward Wilson. Estimate $300/500 Lot 30

title: SEEMAN, Berthold. VITI: or an account of a Government Mission to the Vitian or Fijian Islands in the years 186061. Octav
description: SEEMAN, Berthold. VITI: or an account of a Government Mission to the Vitian or Fijian Islands in the years 186061. Octavo, four tinted plates and a folding engraved map, uncut in original cloth. Cambridge, Macmillan, 1862. Estimate $200/400

title: SHACKLETON, Sir Ernest Henry.
description: SHACKLETON, Sir Ernest Henry. THE HEART OF THE ANTARCTIC: Being the Story of the British Antarctic Expedition 1907 – 1909. Two volumes, thick octavo, coloured and black & white plates, folding maps and panorama laid to linen, rebound in modern blue cloth, gilt, preserving the cloth of the original silver decorated front boards, with old paper library label, top edge gilt. London, William Heinemann, 1909. First edition of the official account of Shackleton’s British Antarctic Expedition, 1907 – 1909, in the Nimrod, one of the greatest of all Antarctic expeditions, which arguably made greater advances in Antarctic exploration than all previous expeditions. Estimate $200/300

title: WEBSTER, John. LAST CRUISE OF THE WANDERER. Octavo, original patterned cloth, gilt: presentation copy, inscribed and sig
description: WEBSTER, John. LAST CRUISE OF THE WANDERER. Octavo, original patterned cloth, gilt: presentation copy, inscribed and signed on a preliminary blank leaf. Sydney, F. Cunninghame, [1863]. Rare. Webster’s account of the last adventure and dramatic death of Ben Boyd on this voyage to establish a republic in Papua. Ferguson, 18285 (with a long annotation). Estimate $300/500 Lot 35

title: WEBBER, John. A TOOPAPAOO OF A CHIEF, WITH A PRIEST MAKING HIS OFFERING TO THE MORAI, IN HOEHEINE [with] WAHEIADOOA, CHI
description: WEBBER, John. A TOOPAPAOO OF A CHIEF, WITH A PRIEST MAKING HIS OFFERING TO THE MORAI, IN HOEHEINE [with] WAHEIADOOA, CHIEF OF OHEITEPEHA, LYING IN STATE. Two original handcoloured aquatint plates, images approximately 285 x 415 mm, one without watermark and the second (handled and with short splits at blank foot, paper strengthened verso) with J. Whatman 1820 watermark, with accompanying leaves of descriptive text, respectively Wilmott 1819, and J. Whatman 1819 watermarks. London, Published by Boydell and Co., 1809 [but circa 1820]. Two scarce plates from Webber’s Views in the South Seas, “the only colour plate book relating to Cook’s third voyage, and the last of the great Cook publications” (Ellis catalogue). First published by John and Joseph Boydell in about 1809, the work was issued by them and their successors, Hurst and Robinson, well into the 1820s. See Abbey, 595; Forbes, 397; Hill 2, 1837; Holmes, 79; Kroepelien, 1341; Tooley English Books, 501; Wantrup (2025), 12.17. Estimate $800/1200

title: WILD, Frank. SHACKLETON’S LAST VOYAGE. The story of the Quest… from the official journal and private diary kept by Dr A. H. Macklin.
description: WILD, Frank. SHACKLETON’S LAST VOYAGE. The story of the Quest… from the official journal and private diary kept by Dr A. H. Macklin. Thick octavo, colour frontispiece and numerous photographic illustrations and maps, scattered pale foxing, original gilt-decorated pictorial cloth New York, Frederick A. Stokes Company, 1923. First US edition. + MILL, Hugh Robert. THE LIFE OF SIR ERNEST SHACKLETON. Octavo, map and illustrations, original cloth, gilt. London, William Heinemann Ltd., 1923. Estimate $200/400

title: ALLEN, Charles H. A VISIT TO QUEENSLAND AND HER GOLDFIELDS. Octavo, uncut in original giltdecorated green cloth, recased.
description: ALLEN, Charles H. A VISIT TO QUEENSLAND AND HER GOLDFIELDS. Octavo, uncut in original giltdecorated green cloth, recased. London, Chapman and Hall, 1870. First edition: author’s presentation copy to his son. Includes a good section on the author’s visit to Melbourne and Ballarat. Ferguson, 5867. Estimate $200/300

title: BACKHOUSE, James. A NARRATIVE OF A VISIT TO THE AUSTRALIAN COLONIES. Octavo, with 15 etchings (one folding) and three fo
description: BACKHOUSE, James. A NARRATIVE OF A VISIT TO THE AUSTRALIAN COLONIES. Octavo, with 15 etchings (one folding) and three folding maps (“Tasmania or Van Diemen’s Land”, “New South Wales”, “The World on Mercator’s Projection”), gilt decorated morocco, edges gilt, endpapers renewed, original front free endpaper loosely inserted. London and York, Hamilton, Adams, and Co., 1843. Presentation copy (and uncommon thus): inscribed by the author on the retained free front endpaper to Edward Sayce of Port Phillip. Estimate $400/600

title: BASEDOW, Herbert. “ANTHROPOLOGICAL NOTES on the western coastal tribes of the Northern Territory of South Australia” in
description: BASEDOW, Herbert. “ANTHROPOLOGICAL NOTES on the western coastal tribes of the Northern Territory of South Australia” in Transactions and Proceedings and Report of the Royal Society of South Australia Vol. XXXI). Octavo, plates including 2 colour lithographs, original wrappers, front wrapper detached. Adelaide, 1907. + BASEDOW, Herbert. “ANTHROPOLOGICAL NOTES … North-West Prospecting Expedition, 1903”, in Transactions and Proceedings, Vol. XXVIII, 1904. Octavo, plates including 10 colour lithographs, original wrappers. Adelaide, 1904. Estimate $200/400

title: BASEDOW, Herbert. “NARRATIVE OF AN EXPEDITION of Exploration in North-Western Australia” [in] Proceedings of the Royal G
description: BASEDOW, Herbert. “NARRATIVE OF AN EXPEDITION of Exploration in North-Western Australia” [in] Proceedings of the Royal Geographical Society of Australasia, South Australian Branch... Vol. XVIII. Octavo, plates, original wrappers. Adelaide, W.K. Thomas & Co., 1918. With the scarce “SKETCH PLAN OF THE NORTH-WEST COAST OF AUSTRALIA”, issued in a separate envelope with Vol. XVIII of the Proceedings. Estimate $200/300

title: BASEDOW, Herbert. “PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY AND GEOLOGY OF THE WESTERN RIVERS’ DISTRICT, Northern Territory of Australia” [in]
description: BASEDOW, Herbert. “PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY AND GEOLOGY OF THE WESTERN RIVERS’ DISTRICT, Northern Territory of Australia” [in] Proceedings of the Royal Geographical Society of Australasia, South Australian Branch, Vol. XVI. Octavo, folding maps, with plates and illustrations, original wrappers. Adelaide, The Advertiser Office, 1916. + BASEDOW, Herbert. “JOURNAL OF THE GOVERNMENT NORTH-WEST EXPEDITION” [in] Proceedings of the Royal Geographical Society of Australasia, South Australian Branch, Vol. XV. Octavo, maps, plates and illustrations, original wrappers. Adelaide, W.K. Thomas, 1915. Estimate $200/300

title: BASEDOW, Herbert. JOURNAL OF THE GOVERNMENT NORTH-WEST EXPEDITION. Octavo, with plates and large folding map, original wrappers, fine.
description: BASEDOW, Herbert. JOURNAL OF THE GOVERNMENT NORTH-WEST EXPEDITION. Octavo, with plates and large folding map, original wrappers, fine. Adelaide, Royal Geographical Society of Australasia, South Australian Branch, 1914. First edition. An important expedition, scientifically and anthropologically, under the leadership of L.A. Wells that linked “together the areas traversed by the Horn and Elder Expeditions”. See Greenway, 729. + SKETCH PLAN OF THE NORTH-WEST COAST OF AUSTRALIA to accompany An Expedition of Exploration by Dr. Herbert Basedow 1916. Large folding lithographed map in colour, with inset geological sketch plan, approximately 48 x 75 cm., in printed envelope as issued. Adelaide, R.G.S.S.A., 1917. The map was issued to accompany the journal of Basedow’s second expedition, undertaken in April-June 1916, in search of minerals in the Kimberleys, North-west Australia. + BASEDOW, Herbert. PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY AND GEOLOGY of the Western Rivers’ District, Northern Territory of Australia. Octavo, plates, illustrations, original wrappers. Adelaide, 1916. Estimate $160/220

title: BROWN, H.Y.L. REPORTS ON ARLTUNGA GOLDFIELD, … and Hart’s Range Mica Field.
description: BROWN, H.Y.L. REPORTS ON ARLTUNGA GOLDFIELD, … and Hart’s Range Mica Field. Foolscap folio, four folding geological maps in colour, one plate, detached from original wrappers (friable and splitting at foot, sellotaped at gutter) in later Mackaness morocco. Adelaide, C.E. Bristow, Government Printer, 1897. + BROWN, H.Y.L. REPORT ON GOLD DISCOVERIES near Winnecke’s Depot and Mines on the Arltunga Goldfields, Macdonnell Ranges. Foolscap folio, large folding sketch map, loosely inserted in original wrappers (small splits sellotaped). Adelaide, C.E. Bristow, Government Printer, 1903. Estimate $100/200

title: BROWN, H.Y.L. GOVERNMENT GEOLOGIST’S REPORT on the Tanami Gold Country, with plans.
description: BROWN, H.Y.L. GOVERNMENT GEOLOGIST’S REPORT on the Tanami Gold Country, with plans. Folio, three folding geological maps in colour, one folding plan, a fine copy in original wrappers. Adelaide, Government Printer, 1909. Scarce. + BROWN, H.Y.L. REPORT ON GEOLOGICAL EXPLORATIONS in the West and North-West of South Australia. Foolscap folio, folding geological map in colour, three plates, original wrappers (final plate and rear wrapper slightly rippled). Adelaide, Bristow, 1905. + Three geological reports, including maps and plans, on the Barossa, Lake Eyre, and Mount Amherst (East Kimberley). Estimate $400/600

title: BROWN, Henry Yorke Lyell.
description: BROWN, Henry Yorke Lyell. NORTHERN TERRITORY OF SOUTH AUSTRALIA, NORTH-WESTERN DISTRICT. Reports (Geological and General) resulting from the Explorations Made by the Government Geologist and Staff during 1905. Foolscap folio, two folding maps and three folding plans, two full-page plates and numerous illustrations in the text, original wrappers. Adelaide, C.E. Bristow, Government Printer, 1906. First edition: an important and very scarce paper with much on the Aborigines, the history and exploration of the Northern Territory and the near islands. The paper includes sections by Herbert Basedow, Robert Etheridge, junior, and L.C.E. Gee. Of special interest are Gee’s long narrative journal of the party’s explorations and Basedow’s article on Chinese methods of mining in the Territory and his history of the early days of Territory mining. McLaren, 5402 (miscollated); Mills, 458 and R161. Estimate $300/400

title: BURGESS, H.T. (editor).
description: BURGESS, H.T. (editor). THE CYCLOPEDIA OF SOUTH AUSTRALIA. An Historical and Commercial Review. Descriptive and Biographical, Facts, Figures, and Illustrations. An Epitome of Progress. Two volumes, quarto, illustrations, original half morocco. Adelaide, The Cyclopedia Company, 1907-1909. Estimate $200/400

title: CAPPER, Henry. SOUTH AUSTRALIA. Containing Hints to Emigrants; Proceedings of the South Australian Company; a variety of
description: CAPPER, Henry. SOUTH AUSTRALIA. Containing Hints to Emigrants; Proceedings of the South Australian Company; a variety of useful and authentic information; a map of the Eastern Coast of Gulf St. Vincent, and a plan of Adelaide. Second Edition, considerably augmented. Octavo, folding frontispiece, folding table, original plum cloth, spine and rear board faded and spotted. London, Robert Tyas, 1838. Second edition: author’s presentation copy, inscribed in June in the year of publication to R. Barton (likely Russell Barton on the eve of his family’s emigration to Adelaide in 1839), with Barton’s armorial bookplate: also with the stamp of the Col. Com. For South Australia, May 31, 1838. Ferguson, 2452. Estimate $300/500

title: COTTER, Thomas Young. THE SOUTH AUSTRALIAN ALMANACK and General Directory for 1843. Duodecimo, original semi-limp cloth, with paper label.
description: COTTER, Thomas Young. THE SOUTH AUSTRALIAN ALMANACK and General Directory for 1843. Duodecimo, original semi-limp cloth, with paper label. Adelaide, James Allen, (1843). Ferguson, 3701. Signed on the title page by the early Adelaide artist and lawyer J[ohn] M[ichael] Skipper, and with his inked notes in the Calendar, and on rear endpapers. Estimate $300/500

title: DALY, Mrs Dominic. DIGGING, SQUATTING, AND PIONEERING LIFE in the Northern Territory of South Australia.
description: DALY, Mrs Dominic. DIGGING, SQUATTING, AND PIONEERING LIFE in the Northern Territory of South Australia. Octavo, with a folding tinted map, uncut in the original decorated cloth, hinges taped. London, Sampson Low, Marston, Searle & Rivington, 1887. First edition: a valuable account of the foundation years of Northern Territory settlement, from 1870 to 1887, by the Governor’s daughter-in-law. Ferguson, 8939. Estimate $140/240

title: DAVIDSON, Allan Arthur.
description: DAVIDSON, Allan Arthur. JOURNAL OF EXPLORATIONS IN CENTRAL AUSTRALIA, by The Central Australian Exploration Syndicate, Limited. 1898-1900. Foolscap folio, two large folding maps, (some sellotape repairs), stapled as issued. Adelaide, C.E. Bristow, Government Printer, 1905. Rare: an important commercial and scientific expedition to examine one of the few regions still unexplored at the end of the nineteenth-century, the land lying between the Stuart Highway at Tennant Creek and the Western Australian border. McLaren, 7723 Estimate $400/800

title: [DUTTON] 2,000 MILES OF ROADLESS COUNTRY ACROSS AUSTRALIA Successfully Travelled by a Talbot Motor Car Driven by Mr.
description: [DUTTON] 2,000 MILES OF ROADLESS COUNTRY ACROSS AUSTRALIA Successfully Travelled by a Talbot Motor Car Driven by Mr. H.H. Dutton and M. Aunger. Broadsheet, 380 x 250 mm, photographic illustrations, old folds. Adeliade, “The Advertiser” Print, circa 1909. Advertisement flyer produced by Lewis Motor House, Adelaide. + A snapshot of the Talbot motor car being driven by Dutton’s sons during the 1958 re-enactment. Estimate $200/400

title: DAVIS John. TRACKS OF McKINLAY AND PARTY ACROSS AUSTRALIA. By John Davis, one of the party.
description: DAVIS John. TRACKS OF McKINLAY AND PARTY ACROSS AUSTRALIA. By John Davis, one of the party. Edited ... by William Westgarth. Octavo, with lithograph plates and folding map (loosely inserted), original cloth, uneven fading, rubbed, recased with new endpapers, edges uncut. London, Sampson Low, Son, & Co., 1863. First edition of the only substantial publication relating to the McKinlay expedition in search of Burke and Wills. In a sense the ‘formal’ narrative of the expedition, it was based on the journals of John K. Davis, a member of the expedition. Ferguson, 9005; Wantrup (2023), 180. Estimate $600/800

title: DE FREYCINET, Louis. Thomas CULLITY (translated by).
description: DE FREYCINET, Louis. Thomas CULLITY (translated by). REFLECTIONS ON NEW SOUTH WALES 17881839. Quarto, eight colour and 20 black and white illustrations, original cloth with paper titling panel on front board, without dustwrapper as issued. Sydney, Hordern House, 2001. Edition limited to 300 copies only. Estimate $200/300

title: EARL, George Samuel Windsor.
description: EARL, George Samuel Windsor. ENTERPRISE IN TROPICAL AUSTRALIA. Octavo, with two folding maps (one handcoloured in outline), and four pages of publisher’s advertisements, rebacked in original cloth with new endpapers. London, Madden and Malcolm, 1846. First edition: scarce account of the second attempted settlement of Port Essington on the Cobourg Peninsula from 1838 to 1849, generally acknowledged to be the best eye-witness report. Ferguson, 4268.+ Three works on Queensland and Northern Territory by Marsh, Makin, and Baume. Estimate $200/300

title: EYRE, Edward John. JOURNALS OF EXPEDITIONS OF DISCOVERY INTO CENTRAL AUSTRALIA, and overland from Adelaide to King Georg
description: EYRE, Edward John. JOURNALS OF EXPEDITIONS OF DISCOVERY INTO CENTRAL AUSTRALIA, and overland from Adelaide to King George’s Sound, in the years 1840-1. Two volumes, octavo, with plates, lacking the two rare folding maps (supplied in facsimile), non-uniform original embossed cloth, both volumes rebacked and the hinges sealed with paper tape, Harold Sheard copy with his bookplates. London, T. & W. Boone, 1845. See Ferguson 4031; Wantrup (2023), 133a. Estimate $600/800

title: FLINDERS, Matthew. MATTHEW FLINDERS PRIVATE JOURNAL, from 17 December 1803 at Isle of France to 10 July 1814 at London.
description: FLINDERS, Matthew. MATTHEW FLINDERS PRIVATE JOURNAL, from 17 December 1803 at Isle of France to 10 July 1814 at London. Edited and with an introduction by Anthony J. Brown and Gillian Dooley, Foreword by Witgar Hitchcock, Preface by Paul Brunton. Small quarto, colour portrait and plates, folding map in endpocket, original cloth. Adelaide, Friends of the State Library of South Australia, 2005. The first transcription of this private journal, previously published only in a facsimile of the original manuscript. Estimate $100/160

title: FLINDERS, Matthew. A VOYAGE TO TERRA AUSTRALIS; undertaken for the purpose of completing the discovery of that vast coun
description: FLINDERS, Matthew. A VOYAGE TO TERRA AUSTRALIS; undertaken for the purpose of completing the discovery of that vast country, and prosecuted in the years 1801, 1802, and 1803. Two text volumes, quarto, and folio atlas, plates in the text volumes toned as usual and with oxidised margins, the text uncut and unpressed, clean, a little pale spotting, bound without half titles in old half calf; atlas (approximately 480 x 360 mm.) of folding and double page engraved first issue charts, coastal views, and botanical plates, some repairs at folds, a couple strengthened on verso margins, tiny splits at some folds and in one case at plate mark, a few pencilled notes on two maps, a touch of offsetting, later half calf and marbled boards. London, Nicol, 1814. Rare. The first edition of Flinders’s monumental work, complete with the rare Atlas. Flinders was the first to circumnavigate the continent, finally establishing that Australia was one large island or continent and not, as had previously been suspected, divided by a navigable central strait. This is the official account of his voyage in the Investigator. Although mortally ill, Flinders spent the last years of his too short life preparing this detailed record of the Investigator voyage and of his later voyages in the Porpoise and the Cumberland. Robert Brown’s “General Remarks… on the Botany of Terra Australis”, which is illustrated by Ferdinand Bauer’s botanical plates in the atlas, is printed in an appendix in the second volume, while the text volumes are illustrated by William Westall. Flinders’s charts in the atlas were of such accuracy that they continued to be issued by the Admiralty for decades and form the basis of all modern charts of Australia. The charts in this copy are all first issue. Davidson, pp. 121-3; Ferguson, 576 (miscounting preliminaries in vol. 1); New Hill, 614; Tooley, pp. 77-9; Wantrup (2023), 67a and pp. 181-8. Estimate $20,000/30,000

title: FLINDERS, Matthew. A VOYAGE TO TERRA AUSTRALIS; undertaken for the purpose of completing the discovery of that vast coun
description: FLINDERS, Matthew. A VOYAGE TO TERRA AUSTRALIS; undertaken for the purpose of completing the discovery of that vast country, and prosecuted in the years 1801, 1802, and 1803... Three volumes, quarto (text) and matching portfolio (atlas), plates in the text volumes, and charts, coastal views, and botanical plates in the atlas portfolio, original half leather in felt-lined timber box. Adelaide, South Australian Government Printer, 1989. Facsimile edition limited to 500 sets. Estimate $400/600

title: FORREST, Alexander. WESTERN AUSTRALIA. NORTH-WEST EXPLORATION. Progress Report of Expedition from DeGrey River to Beagle Bay.
description: FORREST, Alexander. WESTERN AUSTRALIA. NORTH-WEST EXPLORATION. Progress Report of Expedition from DeGrey River to Beagle Bay. Foolscap folio, folding lithograph map. Perth, Richard Pether, Government Printer, 1879. One (of three) notably rare papers relating to Forrest’s most important expedition from DeGrey to Port Darwin. Paper no. 31. Estimate $300/500

title: FORREST, John. EXPLORATIONS IN AUSTRALIA: I. – Explorations in search of Dr.
description: FORREST, John. EXPLORATIONS IN AUSTRALIA: I. – Explorations in search of Dr. Leichhardt and Party. II. – From Perth to Adelaide, around the Great Australian Bight. III. – From Champion Bay, Across the Desert to the Telegraph and to Adelaide. With an Appendix on the Condition of Western Australia… Illustrations by G.F. Angas. Octavo, with advertisements, frontispiece portrait and seven other plates, four folding coloured maps, sewing loosening, adhesion mark on endpaper, original green cloth (rubbed) over bevelled boards, lettered and decorated in gilt and black. London, Sampson Low, Marston, Low, & Searle, 1875. First edition of Forrest’s narrative of the first crossing of the continent from the west coast to the Telegraph Line. Ferguson, 9681; Wantrup (2023), 200. Estimate $700/900

title: GEORGE, F.R. and W.R. MURRAY. JOURNAL (WITH PLANS) OF THE GOVERNMENT PROSPECTING EXPEDITION to the South-Western Portion
description: GEORGE, F.R. and W.R. MURRAY. JOURNAL (WITH PLANS) OF THE GOVERNMENT PROSPECTING EXPEDITION to the South-Western Portions of the Northern Territory, by F.R. George; and to the Buxton and Davenport Ranges by W.R. Murray. Foolscap folio, pp. 24 + three folding coloured maps, stapled, loose as issued. Adelaide, C.E. Bristow, 1907. Very scarce: a highly detailed account of the expedition that traversed the country between the Petermann and Treuer Ranges to Tanami by camel in the twelve months from September 1905 to September 1906. The leader, F.R. George, died in the course of the expedition and it was continued under the command of W.R. Murray. Estimate $500/700

title: GILES, Ernest. AUSTRALIA TWICE TRAVERSED. The romance of exploration, being a narrative compiled from the journals of fi
description: GILES, Ernest. AUSTRALIA TWICE TRAVERSED. The romance of exploration, being a narrative compiled from the journals of five exploring expeditions into and through Central Australia, and Western Australia, from 1872 to 1876, Two volumes, octavo, with maps and plates, original pictorial cloth (of closely matched but not identical colour), one rear board with short scratch. London, Sampson Low, 1889. First edition. Ferguson, 9914; Wantrup (2023), 202a. Estimate $900/1200

title: GILL, Thomas. COLONEL WILLIAM LIGHT: Founder of Adelaide.
description: GILL, Thomas. COLONEL WILLIAM LIGHT: Founder of Adelaide. Sailor Soldier Artist, and First SurveyorGeneral of South Australia. Octavo, two folding maps, two folding facsimile documents, and 15 leaves of plates, original publisher’s vellum over bevelled boards, elaborately gilt, top edge gilt, others uncut: a fine copy. Adelaide, R.E.E. Rogers, Government Printer, 1911. First edition thus: deluxe edition on hand-made paper and specially bound of the reproduction of the rare first edition of Light’s A Brief Journal of the Proceedings of William Light, following Thomas Gill’s biography. This is number 175 of 200 numbered and signed copies on handmade paper and in a special binding. ANB, 17368. + The Diary of William Light in Switzerland 1826 (Lyndoch, The Pump Press, 1991). Estimate $140/240

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas, F.R. Nixon, Samuel Calvert, and O. Korn.
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas, F.R. Nixon, Samuel Calvert, and O. Korn. 14 VIEWS OF OLD ADELAIDE FROM SKETCHES IN 1840 – 1849 by S.T. Gill, F.R. Nixon, S. Calvert & O. Korn. Oblong octavo, tinted lithographed titleleaf with added gilt, 14 tinted lithographs, some spotting of blank margins, with the index leaf to the view of North Terrace, and three terminal leaves of subscribers, original half roan and gilt-lettered cloth (stained at head, corners rubbed, the spine renewed). Adelaide, E.S. Wigg & Son, no date, circa 1876. First edition: Ferguson notes, on George Robertson’s authority, that only 200 copies were printed. See Ferguson 9924e. Estimate $400/600

title: GREGORY, A.C. NORTH AUSTRALIAN EXPLORING EXPEDITION: Copy Correspondence [and] Copy of Additional Correspondence.
description: GREGORY, A.C. NORTH AUSTRALIAN EXPLORING EXPEDITION: Copy Correspondence [and] Copy of Additional Correspondence. Two pieces [plus others], foolscap folio, later cloth backed marbled boards. Melbourne, John Ferres, 1855. Scarce: preparatory to Gregory’s great North Australian Expedition; includes letters from Charles Sturt and John Lort Stokes. BOUND with Commander NORMAN. EXPLORATION EXPEDITION. LETTER FROM COMMANDER NORMAN, reporting the return of the “Victoria” from the Gulf of Carpentaria; together with Reports and Correspondence. [with] EXPLORATION EXPEDITION. REPORT OF COMMANDER NORMAN, of H.M.C.S. “Victoria,” together with Copy of his Journal on the Late Expedition to the Gulf of Carpentaria. Melbourne, John Ferris, 1862. Complete papers of the Victorian Northern Search Expeditions. The papers include reports of the inland expeditions of both Landsborough and Walker – the only complete publication of Walker’s reports. Estimate $300/500

title: GREY, George. JOURNALS OF TWO EXPEDITIONS OF DISCOVERY IN NORTH-WEST AND WESTERN AUSTRALIA, during the years 1837, 38, a
description: GREY, George. JOURNALS OF TWO EXPEDITIONS OF DISCOVERY IN NORTH-WEST AND WESTERN AUSTRALIA, during the years 1837, 38, and 39, Under the Authority of Her Majesty’s Government. Describing many newly discovered, important, and fertile Districts, with Observations on the moral and physical Condition of the Aboriginal Inhabitants, &c. &c. By George Grey, Esq. Governor of South Australia; Late Captain of the Eighty-third Regiment. Two volumes, octavo, with two large folding maps loose in an endpocket in volume one, with 22 plates (six coloured), advertisement leaf in volume one, with early owner’s signature of G. Hance on both titles; entirely uncut in the original primary dark violet cloth, the spines very lightly faded, an uncommonly fine and bright copy. London, T. & W. Boone, 1841. First edition: a classic of Western Australian exploration. One of the finest copies we have seen, perhaps rivalling even the Phillipps copy (which was in the same issue binding). Bagnall, 2336; Ferguson, 3228; Richards, 97; Wantrup (2023), 131. See also Jonathan Wantrup, Thomas and William Boone’s Library of Australian Travels (Melbourne, 2019). Estimate $4000/6000

title: HANN, William. REPORT FROM MR. W. HANN, Leader of the Northern Expedition Party.
description: HANN, William. REPORT FROM MR. W. HANN, Leader of the Northern Expedition Party. Foolscap folio, pp. 14; stitched as issued, a touch of pale foxing, very good or better. Brisbane, James C. Beal, Government Printer, 1873. Very scarce: first edition. William Hann’s Northern Expedition set off from Mount Surprise, west of Townsville, on 26 June 1872, instructed to explore Cape York above the 14th parallel to determine its agricultural and mineral potential Although hampered by the poor bushcraft of his subordinates, Hann discovered and named the Tate, Daintree, and Palmer Rivers. It was his discovery of traces of gold on the Palmer that led to the explosive gold rush there. Johnston-Zerner, B204-5; McLaren, 9549-50. Estimate $150/300

title: HANSLOW, F.G. Chippendale (ed.).
description: HANSLOW, F.G. Chippendale (ed.). AUSTRALIAN CYCLING ANNUAL. A Complete Record of Australian Cycling and Other Interesting Information. Octavo, illustrations, first advertisement leaf partly detached, with the original illustrated wrappers, early full calf, gilt. Sydney, George Robertson & Co., 1897. First year of issue and rare. Presented to the North Adelaide Cycling Club in 1935, by W.H.N. Steed. A member of the Club since early 1890s, and for a long period its Honorary Secretary, Steed has made annotations, included a loosely inserted note, and signed the copy twice. Estimate $800/1200 Lot 68

title: HILL, Eva, Florence and Laura (attrib.).
description: HILL, Eva, Florence and Laura (attrib.). THE “STAFF OF LIFE”, a short history of milling, some hints on breadmaking, and a sketch of the career of John Dunn. Octavo, tinted lithograph portrait frontispiece, original embossed red cloth, gilt, foot of spine barely faded from damp. Adelaide, Sands & McDougall, 1883. Dunn emigrated from Devonshire to Glenelg in 1840 and built the colony’s first windmill. Ferguson, 10153. Estimate $100/200

title: HORN, W.A. NOTES BY A NOMAD. An Olla-Podrida.
description: HORN, W.A. NOTES BY A NOMAD. An Olla-Podrida. Octavo, black & white plates, original gilt-decorated cloth, spine faded. Melbourne, Melville & Mullen, 1906. + HORN, W.A. BUSH ECHOES. Octavo, some gatherings browned, title leaf detached, original cloth with onlaid illustration. London, Hugh Rees, 1901. Verse. Estimate $100/140

title: HISCOCKS, F.E. & Co. F.S. CARROLL. THE NEW COUNTIES, HUNDREDS, & DISTRICT ATLAS OF SOUTH AUSTRALIA AND NORTHERN TERRITOR
description: HISCOCKS, F.E. & Co. F.S. CARROLL. THE NEW COUNTIES, HUNDREDS, & DISTRICT ATLAS OF SOUTH AUSTRALIA AND NORTHERN TERRITORY, 1876. Folio, with 25 double-page coloured maps and large folding coloured general map, the general map torn and repaired with paper tape, original half roan and cloth boards, corners repaired and spine replaced to match, gilt cloth label on the front board, the endpaper with Ballarat binder J. McHutchison’s blindstamp, pencilled rough sketch on endpaper verso, Signed on the title by W.H. Coombs, Gawler Parsonage, and with a later owner’s name. Adelaide, E.S. Wigg & Sons, 1876. Scarce and important. Ferguson, 7981 (and, absurdly, 7982). Estimate $800/1200

title: HOWITT, Alfred William.
description: HOWITT, Alfred William. THE NATIVE TRIBES OF SOUTH-EAST AUSTRALIA. Octavo, plates, illustrations, folding maps and folding table, a fine copy in original gilt-decorated green cloth, edges uncut. London, Macmillan, 1904. First edition. Estimate $300/500

title: HURLEY, Frank. PEARLS AND SAVAGES. Adventures in the Air, on Land and Sea- in New Guinea.
description: HURLEY, Frank. PEARLS AND SAVAGES. Adventures in the Air, on Land and Sea- in New Guinea. Large octavo, plates, original cloth, top edge gilt, with bookplate and owner’s name. London and New York, G.P. Putnam’s Sons, 1924. Estimate $100/140

title: JACKSON, Andrew. ROBERT O’HARA BURKE and the Australian Exploring Expedition of 1860. Octavo, engraved title-page, one f
description: JACKSON, Andrew. ROBERT O’HARA BURKE and the Australian Exploring Expedition of 1860. Octavo, engraved title-page, one folding map (few repairs), with 16 pages of advertisements dated November 1862 following the text, original green blind-stamped cloth, Bernard Gore Brett copy with bookplate. London, Smith, Elder and Co., 1862. First edition. Ferguson, 10857; Wantrup (2023), 173. Estimate $200/400

title: JAMES, Thomas Horton. SIX MONTHS IN SOUTH AUSTRALIA with some account of Port Philip and Portland Bay, in Australia Feli
description: JAMES, Thomas Horton. SIX MONTHS IN SOUTH AUSTRALIA with some account of Port Philip and Portland Bay, in Australia Felix; With Advice to Emigrants; to which is added a Monthly Calendar of Gardening and Agriculture, adapted to the climate and seasons. Octavo, folding map of Port Lincoln as frontispiece and another map of Encounter Bay (not noted by Ferguson), early half calf, marbled boards and edges. London, Cross, 1838. First edition, first issue without the four-page 1839 postscript. In addition to being an important early work on the Port Phillip District, James’s work includes the journals of several private expeditions undertaken in the early years of settlement, including an account of Hawdon’s famous overlanding expedition as well as other expeditions to Encounter Bay, Lake Alexandrina and to the River Murray. Ferguson, 2525. Estimate $200/400

title: JONES, Henry Berkeley.
description: JONES, Henry Berkeley. ADVENTURES IN AUSTRALIA in 1852 and 1853. Octavo, original gilt and decorated cloth, worn and repaired on spine, edges uncut, H.L. White copy with Belltrees bookplate. London, Richard Bentley, 1853. First edition: Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria, with much information on the state of the diggings in 1852-3. Ferguson, 10990; Wantrup (2023), 453. Estimate $140/240

title: LANDSBOROUGH, William.
description: LANDSBOROUGH, William. JOURNAL OF LANDSBOROUGH’S EXPEDITION from Carpentaria, in search of Burke and Wills. Octavo, frontispiece, short split in the large folding map, original cloth-backed card wrappers. Melbourne, Wilson & Mackinnon, 1862. First edition. Ferguson, 11329; Wantrup (2023), 174a. Estimate $300/400

title: LINDSAY, David. JOURNAL OF THE ELDER SCIENTIFIC EXPLORING EXPEDITION, 1891. Folio, with two large folding coloured maps
description: LINDSAY, David. JOURNAL OF THE ELDER SCIENTIFIC EXPLORING EXPEDITION, 1891. Folio, with two large folding coloured maps (one with a sealed 4cm. tear), later cloth backed papered boards. Adelaide, Ordered by the House of Assembly to be printed, 1893. Very scarce: the official printing – only 750 printed – of the leader’s report of this elaborate scientific expedition, equipped at the sole expense of Sir Thomas Elder, to explore the unknown interior between Adelaide and the west coast. Beset by internal conflicts, the expedition collapsed in chaos, although it had demonstrated that the country was not suitable for settlement. McLaren, 12616. Estimate $800/1200

title: MACDOUGALL, Archibald (publisher).
description: MACDOUGALL, Archibald (publisher). THE SOUTH AUSTRALIAN ALMANACK, and Adelaide and Colonial Directory for 1843. Duodecimo, with advertisements, stab-sewn but now loose in the original semi-limp cloth, with paper label showing an erasure. Adelaide, 1843. Ferguson, 3723. Estimate $200/400

title: McRAE, Alex. WESTERN AUSTRALIA. REPORT... OF A TRIP to the Fitzroy River, from Roebuck Bay, in the year 1866. Foolscap f
description: McRAE, Alex. WESTERN AUSTRALIA. REPORT... OF A TRIP to the Fitzroy River, from Roebuck Bay, in the year 1866. Foolscap folio, folding map, loose as issued. Perth, Richard Pether, 1881. Estimate $200/400

title: MITCHELL, Sir Thomas Livingstone.
description: MITCHELL, Sir Thomas Livingstone. JOURNAL OF AN EXPEDITION INTO THE INTERIOR OF TROPICAL AUSTRALIA, in search of a route from Sydney to the Gulf of Carpentaria. Octavo, with a frontispiece and eleven lithographed plates, seven maps (four folding), bound without advertisements in handsome half blue morocco, top edge gilt. London, Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, 1848. First edition, first issue. This was Mitchell’s full narrative of his fourth and last expedition. Although not successful in its primary objectives, Mitchell’s year-long expedition into tropical Australia opened up large tracts of previously unknown territory and was the first detailed exploration of what would become the colony of Queensland. The fine lithographed plates after Mitchell’s own drawings show his work as a topographical artist at its best. Ferguson, 4828; Richards, 102; Wantrup (2023), 129. Estimate $600/800

title: MORGAN, Lewis H. AUSTRALIAN KINSHIP, from original memoranda of Rev.
description: MORGAN, Lewis H. AUSTRALIAN KINSHIP, from original memoranda of Rev. Lorimer Fison. Octavo, original printed wrappers showing stain from removal of postage stamp, spine and edges chipped, corner of rear wrapper lost. (Boston, 1872). Rare: a seminal offprint from the Proceedings of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. George Taplin’s own copy, addressed to him and with 1873 postal markings on the rear wrapper; subsequently in the collection of George Angas Johnson, with his bookplate. Estimate $400/600

title: MITCHELL, Thomas W. SKI HEIL. Octavo, with 4 plates and numerous illustrations in the text; original art deco illustrated cloth.
description: MITCHELL, Thomas W. SKI HEIL. Octavo, with 4 plates and numerous illustrations in the text; original art deco illustrated cloth. Sydney, Sydney and Melbourne Publishing Co., 1937. First edition of “the first local text book on skiing”: of obvious importance in the history of one of Australia’s most popular sports. This is a surprisingly scarce book, with a memorable and beautifully designed Art Deco cover illustration. The scarcity of the book is perhaps explained by the (innocuous) German title that, in wartime Australia, must have seemed like an invitation to the bonfire. Estimate $100/200

title: NAPIER, Francis. NOTES OF A VOYAGE from New South Wales to the North Coast of Australia, from the Journal of the late Francis Napier.
description: NAPIER, Francis. NOTES OF A VOYAGE from New South Wales to the North Coast of Australia, from the Journal of the late Francis Napier. Octavo, with photographic portrait, eight lithographed plates, four folding maps, one full-page map (p. 70), and a few other illustrations in the text; original green cloth (varnished on spine and upper board), Ingleton copy with booklabel [Glasgow, Privately Printed, 1876]. Extremely scarce. Publisher’s presentation copy of the posthumous first edition of Francis Napier’s journal of Cadell’s 1867-9 Northern Territory Expedition, the only separately-published account. Napier had died in 1875 and his brother James published this book on the basis of his journal and papers for private distribution, without an imprint, in Glasgow in 1876. Ferguson, 13058; Wantrup (2023), 102. Estimate $300/500

title: O’HARA, James. THE HISTORY OF NEW SOUTH WALES. Octavo, an uncut copy with the half-title, original boards (some marking)
description: O’HARA, James. THE HISTORY OF NEW SOUTH WALES. Octavo, an uncut copy with the half-title, original boards (some marking) with later vellum spine and corners, the first and final few gatherings with pale marking, endpapers renewed. London, J. Hatchard, 1818. The first general history of New South Wales and Van Diemen’s Land that is not merely a compilation. “The first true history of the colony... O’Hara provides the best picture of the first half of Macquarie’s rule, the Golden Age, that we have between two covers” (Wantrup). This is the “second” (i.e. third) issue of the first edition: all issues are scarce. Ferguson, 725; Wantrup (2023), 40, and pp. 140-141. Estimate $300/600

title: PLATT. (publisher). PLATTS’S ALMANAC, DIARY, AND SOUTH AUSTRALIAN DIRECTORY for 1851. Octavo, with illustrated advertise
description: PLATT. (publisher). PLATTS’S ALMANAC, DIARY, AND SOUTH AUSTRALIAN DIRECTORY for 1851. Octavo, with illustrated advertisements, original semi-limp cloth-backed card with printed paper label, rear joint split, rear cover peeling, endpapers dusty. Adelaide, Platts’s Library and Wholesale Stationery Warehouse, 1851. Ferguson, 14193. The Diary section is liberally annotated in ink, mainly with details of activities and accounts on a pastoral property. Estimate $300/500

title: PROESCHEL, Frederick. GENERAL, AGRICULTURAL & GOLD FIELDS, MAP OF VICTORIA. Engraved handcoloured folding map, approxima
description: PROESCHEL, Frederick. GENERAL, AGRICULTURAL & GOLD FIELDS, MAP OF VICTORIA. Engraved handcoloured folding map, approximately 530 x 455 mm, mounted on linen as issued (verso with pale foxing), the printed key (lacking title leaf) tipped onto the back board, as issued, and the map folding into the original green cloth, lettered in gilt and decorated in blind. Melbourne, n.d. (circa 1859). Rare: an important map of gold-rush Victoria, with extensive statistics in the borders, and a handsome large vignette of the goldfields and other views engraved by David Tulloch. Proeschel was the first dedicated map publisher in Australia, described by the local press as “the Wyld of Victoria”. He followed gold to Australia in the mid-1850s but returned to Germany in 1864. Apart from several editions of this notable map of Victoria and a similar one for the city of Melbourne, Proeschel specialised in producing single-sheet regional and suburban maps with local advertisements in the borders. “In seven years he produced 30,000 maps but few remain as many were given to customers as disposable items” (Clancy). See Ferguson, 14435 (minor variation); on Proeschel see Clancy, p. 21 (and pp. 170-1, 175). Estimate $1500/2000 Lot 87

title: SEMPLE, James George (alias “Major” and “Lt.
description: SEMPLE, James George (alias “Major” and “Lt. Col.” SEMPLE-LISLE) THE LIFE OF MAJOR J.G. SEMPLE LISLE; containing a faithful narrative of his alternate vicissitudes of splendour and misfortune. Written by Himself… Octavo, frontispiece portrait, old polished calf (dried out on spine). London, W. Stewart, 1799. First edition. An adventurer and confidence trickster, who falsely adopted the rank of a military officer (variously ‘Major” and ‘LtColonel’), Semple was sentenced to transportation to New South Wales on the Lady Shore, on which convict transport he assisted in suppressing a mutiny during the voyage, his account of which is given here. After the mutiny he was returned to Great Britain was quickly in trouble again and by 1799 was still in custody at Tothill Fields. Like Barrington, a notorious character of the time, this “faithful narrative” was almost certainly published for his material benefit. Ferguson, 297. Estimate $140/240

title: SHANN, E.O.G. CATTLE CHOSEN. A Story of the first group settlement in Western Australia 1829 – 1841. Octavo, portrait, p
description: SHANN, E.O.G. CATTLE CHOSEN. A Story of the first group settlement in Western Australia 1829 – 1841. Octavo, portrait, plate and folding plan, original cloth, in dustwrapper. London, Oxford University Press, 1926. First edition: scarce. Fine association copy, with signed inscription in 1927 from Isabel Brockman, grand-daughter of John Bussell the original settler of the homestead. Estimate $100/200

title: SHAW, William. THE LAND OF PROMISE; or, My Impressions of Australia.
description: SHAW, William. THE LAND OF PROMISE; or, My Impressions of Australia. Duodecimo, corner of free endpaper clipped, uncut in original cloth, gilt. London, Simpkin, Marshall, & Co., 1854. First edition. A spirited, anecdotal picture of social and economic conditions on the various diggings. Ferguson, 15620; Wantrup (2023), 420. Estimate $160/220

title: SOUTH AUSTRALIA. FIRST [AND SECOND] REPORT FROM THE SELECT COMMITTEE ON SOUTH AUSTRALIA. Ordered by the House of Commons
description: SOUTH AUSTRALIA. FIRST [AND SECOND] REPORT FROM THE SELECT COMMITTEE ON SOUTH AUSTRALIA. Ordered by the House of Commons, to be Printed, 9 March [and 10 June] 1841. Foolscap folio, four folding handcoloured engraved maps and plans, three of them by Arrowsmith, tape repair to verso fold of first map, the map of Special Surveys in South Australia torn along one long fold, the first report chipped at outer edge and with a Law Society stamp on title, the two Reports bound together with several introductory leaves of House of Lords 1843 Sessional Papers, in one volume, modern quarter cloth and papered boards. (London), 1841. Apart from the inherent importance for the early years of the colony, the Second Report is of interest for the four fine maps which include the surveys of Colonel William Light, as well as two Arrowsmith maps of the South Australian coast recording the most recent surveys improving on Flinders. Ferguson, 3218, and 3219. Estimate $500/800

title: SOUTH AUSTRALIA. IMPROVEMENTS AT PORT ELLIOT, the Goolwa, and Navigation of the Murray.
description: SOUTH AUSTRALIA. IMPROVEMENTS AT PORT ELLIOT, the Goolwa, and Navigation of the Murray. Foolscap folio, two folding lithograph maps with handcoloured outlines, original cloth backed card wrappers with printed label. Adelaide, Government Printer, 1851. Estimate $200/300

title: SOWDEN, William J. THE NORTHERN TERRITORY AS IT IS. A Narrative of the South Australian Parliamentary Party’s Trip, and
description: SOWDEN, William J. THE NORTHERN TERRITORY AS IT IS. A Narrative of the South Australian Parliamentary Party’s Trip, and full description of the Northern Territory; its settlement and industries. By William J. Sowden. With an Appendix, containing reports of the general resources of the Territory by Professor Tate, F.G.S. Octavo, original cloth, gilt. Adelaide, W.K. Thomas & Co., 1882. First edition of this detailed and important account of the Northern Territory written on the basis of the official tour of inspection through the Territory by South Australian parliamentarians after nearly two decades of settlement. Ferguson, 16038. + LITCHFIELD, J.S. FARNORTH MEMORIES. Octavo, plate, original cloth. Sydney, Angus & Robertson, 1930. Estimate $200/400

title: SPENCER, Walter Baldwin (editor).
description: SPENCER, Walter Baldwin (editor). REPORT OF THE WORK OF THE HORN SCIENTIFIC EXPEDITION TO CENTRAL AUSTRALIA. Part I. – Introduction, Narrative, Summary of Results, Supplement to Zoological Report, Map; Part II. – Zoology; Part III. – Geology and Botany; Part IV. – Anthropology. Four parts in four volumes, quarto, corrigenda leaf in volume two, with in total 47 lithographed plates after Spencer, Robert Wendel and others (nine folding and 15, including three of birds, in colour), 22 photographic plates, a large folding lithographed map, woodcuts in the text, contemporary half morocco, spines sunned, front hinge of Part II cracked. London and Melbourne, Dulau and Co., Melville, Mullen and Slade, 1896. First edition: an association copy of the most comprehensive record of a scientific expedition undertaken in Australia in the nineteenth century: each volume signed on the title by F.W. Belt, Horn’s brother-in-law, who accompanied the expedition as a collector and taxidermist, and after whom Mount Francis in the MacDonnell Ranges was named. The four volumes comprise the narrative, zoology, geology and botany, and anthropology. The reports were written by notable Australian scientists of the day, including Professor W. Baldwin Spencer, Professor Ralph Tate, J.A. Watts, J.H. Maiden, E.C. Stirling, Alfred J. North, Walter Frogatt, and Edgar Waite. Completely financed and equipped by William Austin Horn, a wealthy Adelaide philanthropist, who had himself led several short expeditions into the interior in the late 1860s and early 1870s, the expedition examined the country between Oodnadatta and the MacDonnell Ranges under the command of Charles Winnecke. The party was in the field for three months and much useful work was accomplished in anthropology, botany, and zoology. Ferguson, 16071; Greenway, 8672. Estimate $4000/6000

title: SPENCER, Walter Baldwin and Francis James GILLEN. ACROSS AUSTRALIA. Two volumes, octavo, plates (some coloured) and two
description: SPENCER, Walter Baldwin and Francis James GILLEN. ACROSS AUSTRALIA. Two volumes, octavo, plates (some coloured) and two folding maps, a bright copy in original red gilt decorated cloth, top edge gilt. London, Macmillan, 1912. First edition. Spencer and Gillen’s scientific expeditions in Central Australia, which resulted in a series of major scientific texts, were the beginnings of modern Australian anthropological fieldwork. Estimate $300/400

description: STEPHENS, John. THE ROYAL SOUTH AUSTRALIAN ALMANACK and General Directory for 1847. Duodecimo, the text block detached within original cloth-backed wrappers with paper label, early inked notes on the endpapers (crossed through), the Preface, and the Calendar: signed on the front wrapper by the bibliographer and collector Thos. Gill. Adelaide, J. Stephens, 1847. Ferguson, 4637. Estimate $300/500

title: STEPHENS, John. THE HISTORY OF THE RISE AND PROGRESS of the New British Province of South Australia… Octavo, with plates
description: STEPHENS, John. THE HISTORY OF THE RISE AND PROGRESS of the New British Province of South Australia… Octavo, with plates (one stained, several with browned margins) and folding map (several spots), folding table, uncut, original brown cloth. London, Smith, Elder, & Co., 1839. Second issue (“edition”) of Stephens’s Land of Promise… of the same year: inscribed by the author. Ferguson, 2851. Estimate $200/400 Lot 94

title: STOKES, John Lort. DISCOVERIES IN AUSTRALIA; with an account of the Coasts and Rivers explored and surveyed during the V
description: STOKES, John Lort. DISCOVERIES IN AUSTRALIA; with an account of the Coasts and Rivers explored and surveyed during the Voyage of H.M.S. Beagle, In the Years 1837 – 38 – 39 – 40 – 41 – 42 – 43. By Command of the Lords Commissioners of the Admiralty. Also a Narrative of Captain Owen Stanley’s Visits to the Islands in the Arafura Sea. Two volumes, octavo, with 26 plates and eight folding charts (seven in endpocket), front hinge of first volume split and with the sewing loosening at the penultimate gathering, non-uniform original cloth: one volume with the engraved bookplate of Henry Dutton, the second inscribed London, Boone, 1846. First edition. In 1837 John Clements Wickham was sent to survey and complete the discovery of those parts of the northern coast of Australia not already charted by Flinders or King and still known only from the rough charts of Louis de Freycinet. Wickham was also instructed to improve the charts of key areas of the coast such as Torres Strait, Bass Strait and the approaches to the new and developing settlements at Adelaide and Swan River, and to search for any large rivers on the north-west coast which, it was hoped, would open up the northern coast and the interior to exploration and further settlement – as part of this larger plan the Beagle transported George Grey’s land party to the north-west coast in 1837. In the course of this expedition Wickham and Stokes completed the discovery of the north-west coast and accurately charted for the first time other stretches of coast. On the northern coast they discovered and partly explored five rivers, while Stokes and his men also undertook many expeditions inland which are recorded in this official account. Ferguson, 4406; Wantrup (2023), 89. Estimate $1200/1600

title: STUART, John McDouall.
description: STUART, John McDouall. EXPLORATIONS IN AUSTRALIA The Journals of John McDouall Stuart during the years 1858, 1859, 1861, & 1862, when he fixed the Centre of the Continent and successfully crossed it from sea to sea. Edited... by William Hardman. Octavo, with an actual photograph as frontispiece, the backing sheet foxed, a sketch map, 12 plates, and the large folding coloured map (renewed at some folds, several ink smudges) in an endpocket, rebacked with the earlier spine, new endpapers. London, Saunders, Otley, 1864. First edition: complete with the folding map omitted by Ferguson in error. This copy signed on the frontispiece verso, bleeding through onto recto, by the orchardist and jam maker Geo. McEwin of Glen Ewin. Ferguson, 16381 (misdescribed); Wantrup (2023), 162a. Estimate $400/600

title: STUART, John McDouall.
description: STUART, John McDouall. JOHN McDOUALL STUART’S EXPLORATIONS across the continent of Australia with charts 1861-62. Octavo, frontispiece large folding map with short tear sealed, some spotting of text as often, later half morocco and marbled boards. Melbourne, F.F. Baillière, 1863. First public edition of Stuart’s journals of his fifth and sixth expeditions in which he succeeded in crossing the continent from south to north. Ferguson, 16380; Wantrup (2023), 161. Estimate $300/400

title: STURT, Charles. TWO EXPEDITIONS INTO THE INTERIOR OF SOUTHERN AUSTRALIA, during the years 1828, 1829, 1830 and 1831: wit
description: STURT, Charles. TWO EXPEDITIONS INTO THE INTERIOR OF SOUTHERN AUSTRALIA, during the years 1828, 1829, 1830 and 1831: with Observations on the Soil, Climate and General Resources of the Colony of New South Wales. Two volumes, octavo, 13 plates (four handcoloured) and two maps, the folding map taped along centre, plates toned, uncut in modern half leather and marbled boards, tightly bound. London, Smith, Elder, 1833. First edition. Sturt’s full narrative of his two crucial expeditions into the interior, an account of over 4000 miles of exploration carried out in four years. Although the news of Sturt’s extensive discoveries had reached Britain within months of his return, with the results reported in various journals, it was this handsome two-volume account that was most responsible for rekindling the subdued interest in Australian discovery and geography. Sturt’s journal was the first full-scale publication of an explorer’s journal since the publication of Oxley’s book thirteen years before. It was a huge success, with a second edition being called for the following year. Among all the explorers of the heroic age of the 1830s and 1840s only the journals of Sturt and Mitchell went to a second edition. Ferguson, 1704; Wantrup (2023), 118a. Estimate $800/1200

title: SUTHERLAND, George. OUR INHERITANCE IN THE HILLS, being a series of articles by a special correspondent.
