description: TEICHELMANN, C.G. and C.W. SCHUERMANN. OUTLINES OF A GRAMMAR, VOCABULARY, AND PHRASEOLOGY, of the Aboriginal Language of South Australia, spoken by the Natives in and for some distance around Adelaide. Octavo, with the errata leaf, modern half morocco and marbled boards, Rollo Hammet copy with his book label. Adelaide, Published by the Authors, at the Native Location [printed by Robert Thomas and Co., Hindley Street, Adelaide], 1840. Rare: the first book on the South Australian Aborigines. Ferguson, 3102. Estimate $400/600

title: TENCH, Captain Watkin.
description: TENCH, Captain Watkin. A NARRATIVE OF THE EXPEDITION TO BOTANY BAY. Octavo, coloured portrait frontispiece, with map and plate, original half navy ox-skin and moiré cloth. Melbourne, Edition Renard, 2004. Edition limited to 212 copies - issue bound in half ox-skin. Estimate $120/240

title: TENCH, Watkin. A COMPLETE ACCOUNT OF THE SETTLEMENT AT PORT JACKSON, in New South Wales, including an accurate descripti
description: TENCH, Watkin. A COMPLETE ACCOUNT OF THE SETTLEMENT AT PORT JACKSON, in New South Wales, including an accurate description of the Situation of the Colony; of the Natives; and of its natural productions: Taken on the spot... Quarto, with folding “Map of the hitherto unexplored country contiguous to Port Jackson…” (foxed), slight loss at two blank corners, bound, without the List of Subscribers as sometimes found, in contemporary calf, marbled endpapers, expertly respined in period style with contrasting spine labels, gilt and decorated. London, G. Nicol and J. Sewell, 1793. First edition. Captain Watkin Tench was the only First Fleet chronicler to publish more than one book. He had returned to England with other marines in the Gorgon in 1792 and his very scarce second account of the colony was published over a year later, at the end of 1793. Tench “completes his account of the first years of the colony and brings his record of events down to the end of the first four years of settlement. The map and text give important and full details of the early expeditions of discovery to the south and to the west, including those which Tench led himself. As an accurate, well-written and acutely observed account of the earliest years of Australia’s colonisation, it is a most important addition to any collection of Australian books. It is rare despite the hundreds of copies that were originally printed…” (Wantrup). Davidson, p. 76; Ferguson, 171; Wantrup (2023), 16. Estimate $8000/10,000 Lots 105 and 116

title: TERRY, Michael. SAND AND SUN: Two Gold-hunting Expeditions with Camels in the Dry Lands of Central Australia.
description: TERRY, Michael. SAND AND SUN: Two Gold-hunting Expeditions with Camels in the Dry Lands of Central Australia. Octavo, plates, a couple of early leaves with light foxing, original cloth, map of the 1932 expedition on the front endpapers and of the 1933 expedition on the back endpapers. London, Michael Joseph Ltd., 1937. First edition: with loosely inserted signed note from the author, and several 1933 newspaper clippings. Explorations in Central Australia undertaken in 1932 and 1933 with Stanley J. O’Grady and Benjamin E. Nicker in the country around Lake Amadeus and Lake Mackay, recently discovered by the Mackay Aerial Survey Expedition. ANB, 43855; Greenway, 9069. + TERRY, Michael. ACROSS UNKONWN AUSTRALIA. Octavo, illustrations, original green cloth. London, Herbert Jenkins, 1925. Estimate $300/500

description: THREADGILL Bessie. SOUTH AUSTRALIAN LAND EXPLORATION. 1856 to 1880. Adelaide, Public Library, Museum, and Art Gallery of South Australia, 1922. Octavo, two volumes, illustrations, folding maps, original wrappers. Estimate $80/120

title: TIETKENS, William Henry.
description: TIETKENS, William Henry. JOURNAL OF MR. W.H. TIETKENS’ CENTRAL AUSTRALIAN EXPLORING EXPEDITION. Journal of the Central Australian Exploring and Prospecting Association’s Expedition, 1889, under Command of William Henry Tietkens [drop title]. [Adelaide], Ordered by the House of Assembly to be printed, 1890. The extremely scarce first official printing in the South Australian parliamentary papers of the leader’s account of this important expedition. Brown. McLaren, 16076. Estimate $400/600

description: VINCENT, J. Matthew. THE AUSTRALIAN IRRIGATION COLONIES on the River Murray, Victoria and South Australia. title: WAKEFIELD, Edward Gibbon.
description: WAKEFIELD, Edward Gibbon. THE NEW BRITISH PROVINCE OF SOUTH AUSTRALIA; or a Description of the Country, Illustrated by Charts and Views; With an Account of the Principles, Objects, Plan, and Prospects of the Colony. Octavo, frontispiece and one plate, one folding map, rebacked original green cloth, new endpapers. London, C. Knight, 1838. Second edition: following the foundation of the colony. + Four works on South Australia. Estimate $200/400

title: WARBURTON, Peter Egerton.
description: WARBURTON, Peter Egerton. JOURNEY ACROSS THE WESTERN INTERIOR OF AUSTRALIA. Octavo, with plates and folding map coloured in outline, repaired tears at the map folds, original gilt pictorial cloth over bevelled boards, label removed from endpaper with glue residue remaining. London, Sampson Low, 1875. First edition: a pleasing association copy of Warburton’s narrative of his expedition from the Telegraph Line to the west coast, the first expedition to cross the continent from east to west. This was the copy of Northern Territory pioneer Aeneas Gunn, with his ownership inscription on the half-title. Aeneas Gunn was a newspaper editor and journalist, husband of Jeannie Gunn, whose classic account of their life in the Territory, We of the Never-Never, was written after Aeneas’s early death. Ferguson, 18187; Wantrup (2023), 201 (‘essential’). Estimate $600/900

title: WENTWORTH, William Charles.
description: WENTWORTH, William Charles. A STATISTICAL, HISTORICAL, AND POLITICAL DESCRIPTION of the Colony of New South Wales, and its Dependent Settlements in Van Diemen’s Land: with a particular enumeration of the advantages which these colonies offer for emigration, and their superiority in many respects over those possessed by the United States of America. By W.C. Wentworth, Esq. a Native of the Colony. Octavo, uncut in original boards (binding broken), lacking backstrip, boxed. London, Printed for G. and W.B. Whittaker, 1819. First edition of this famous book: author’s presentation copy. The first original work published by an Australian-born author, son of a convict mother and a well-connected father who “did not migrate entirely of his own volition” (Richards, diplomatically). Wentworth wrote with the avowed object of encouraging intending emigrants and gives a great deal of information about New South Wales and Van Diemen’s Land, as well as expressing some of his own ideas on the future development of the colony. Ferguson, 771; Wantrup (2023), 53. Estimate $600/900

title: WHITE, John. JOURNAL OF A VOYAGE to New South Wales.
description: WHITE, John. JOURNAL OF A VOYAGE to New South Wales. With sixty-five plates of nondescript animals, birds, lizards, serpents… Quarto, 65 engraved plates, very slight and occasional dust marking at head, endpapers with old creasing, a fine copy in Aquarius binding of speckled half calf and marbled boards, spine gilt and decorated. London, J. Debrett, 1790. First edition of White’s First Fleet journal, the issue with uncoloured plates. John White was the chief surgeon on the First Fleet and Surgeon-general to the settlement, whose most remarkable, if still little recognised, achievement was the minuscule mortality rates among the convicts on the long voyage from England to New South Wales, in what is still one of the largest mass movements of humanity ever undertaken. He continued to overcome severe medical problems in the first settlement, working in atrocious conditions, and even became a pioneer of the use of native Australian plants as medicine. His journal commences with the sailing of the First Fleet, including an account of the voyage from England.
